heroText: Cannes is a compact Riviera city where film-festival glamour, beaches and old-town viewpoints sit close together. Start on La Croisette, climb Le Suquet for harbour views, then use the Palais des Festivals area for event planning. Nice Cote d'Azur Airport is the main gateway, with rail and road links along the coast.

areas.name: La Croisette
areas.text: La Croisette is best for beach hotels, sea views, luxury shopping and quick access to festival venues.

areas.name: Le Suquet
areas.text: Le Suquet is the old-town hill, better for atmosphere, restaurants and harbour views than large resort hotels.

areas.name: Cannes Centre
areas.text: Cannes Centre is practical for the station, shops, restaurants and walking between beaches and event venues.

areas.name: Palm Beach
areas.text: Palm Beach is quieter and more residential, useful for beach access and stays away from the festival core.

stayOverview: Stay on La Croisette for beaches and festival access, Le Suquet for old-town atmosphere, Cannes Centre for station convenience, or Palm Beach for quieter seaside stays away from the busiest event core.
hotelIntro: Cannes hotel choice changes sharply around festival dates. La Croisette and the centre are most convenient, Le Suquet has more character, and Palm Beach works when calmer nights and beach time matter more.
rentalCars: Skip a car inside Cannes; rent only for hill villages, countryside routes or a wider Riviera trip.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Cannes Centre or La Croisette if festival venues, restaurants and the station need to stay walkable.

travelTips.title: Festival timing
travelTips.text: Book very early during Cannes Film Festival, when prices and access change across the whole Riviera.

travelTips.title: Beach choice
travelTips.text: Check whether a hotel uses private beach clubs or public beaches before assuming easy sea access.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Antibes is an easy rail trip for old-town streets, Picasso Museum and a calmer Riviera harbour.

history.label: 2nd century
history.text: By the 2nd century BC, the Ligurian Oxybii established a settlement here known as Aegitna (Ancient Greek: Αἴγιτνα).
In 154 BC, it became the scene of violent but quick conflict between the troops of Quintus Opimius and the Oxybii.

history.label: 10th century
history.text: In the 10th century, the town was known as Canua.

history.label: 11th century
history.text: Construction of a castle in 1035 fortified the city then known as Cannes, and at the end of the 11th century construction was started on two towers on the Lérins islands.
Around 1530, Cannes detached from the monks who had controlled the city for hundreds of years and became independent.

history.label: 19th century
history.text: At the end of the 19th century, several more railways were completed, which prompted the arrival of streetcars.

history.label: 20th century
history.text: In the 20th century, new luxury hotels such as the Carlton, Majestic, Martinez, and JW Marriott Cannes were built.
This casino was demolished and replaced by the new Palace in 1979.
In 2021, Cannes was designated as the City of Film by the UNESCO Creative Cities Network.

history.label: Today
history.text: The area was a fishing village used as a port of call between the Lérins Islands.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Canua was probably the site of a small Ligurian port, and later a Roman outpost on Le Suquet hill, suggested by Roman tombs discovered here.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: After the closure of the Casino des Fleurs (hôtel Gallia), a luxury establishment was built for the rich winter clientele, the Casino Municipal next to the pier Albert-Edouard.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: There were fewer British and German tourists after the First World War, but more Americans.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The city council had the idea of starting an international film festival shortly after World War II.
